name: Bauhaus

influenced_by: Arts and Crafts movement's craft ideals
Constructivism and De Stijl's geometric abstraction

eras: 1919–1933 (school open in Weimar, then Dessau, then Berlin, closed under Nazi pressure)
garments: not primarily a fashion look, though its textile workshop (led largely by women, including Anni Albers) produced influential geometric weaving
reacts_against: the separation of fine art from craft and industry; the school's founding idea was that good design for mass-produced objects was as serious a pursuit as painting, expressed through primary colors, geometric form and new industrial materials (tubular steel, glass).
revivals: directly shaped the Swiss/International Typographic Style and nearly all mid-century modern furniture design that followed
article: Bauhaus color theory is inseparable from the school's founding argument: that there should be no wall between fine art and the design of ordinary, mass-produced things. Founded in Weimar in 1919 by the architect Walter Gropius, the school taught painters, weavers and furniture-makers side by side and pushed its students toward a reduced, geometric visual language built on primary colors (red, yellow, blue), black, white and grey, and the basic forms of circle, square and triangle — partly inherited from Constructivism and De Stijl, partly developed in-house by teachers like Wassily Kandinsky and Josef Albers, who spent decades studying how colors interact. The school's most famous object, Marcel Breuer's tubular-steel Wassily Chair (1925), shows the whole philosophy at once: industrial material, geometric reduction, no applied ornament. Political pressure forced the Bauhaus to close in 1933, and many of its teachers emigrated to the United States, where they taught a generation of American designers directly — which is the main reason Bauhaus's red-yellow-blue, black-and-white geometric language became the default grammar of so much 20th-century graphic design, furniture and architecture rather than staying a short-lived German experiment.

wiki_facts.key_motifs: Geometric shapes (circles, squares, triangles), clean lines, sans-serif typography, abstract forms, lack of ornamentation, industrial materials (steel, glass, concrete)
wiki_facts.key_colours: Primary colors (red, yellow, blue), black, white, gray
